articles.title: After fight with husband at temple, woman sets herself, 2 sons ablaze in Tamil Nadu
articles.summary: Madurai: A 28-year-old woman and her two sons, 5 and 3, died after she allegedly set herself and the children on fire following a family dispute in Tenkasi.
articles.body: Madurai: A 28-year-old woman and her two young sons died after she allegedly set herself and the children on fire following a family dispute near Sivagiri in Tenkasi district on Monday.The deceased were Mariammal of Vadakkuchathiram West Street, and her sons Kabineshwaran, 5, and Rabineshwaran, 3. Mariammal was married to Kalipandi, 30, a painter, for six years. Kabineshwaran was a Class I student at a govt school, while Rabineshwaran attended an anganwadi centre.Police said Kalipandi was addicted to alcohol and frequently quarreled with his wife. The incident occurred after Mariammal took her children to a temple festival at Vadakkuchathiram. She also participated in a kummi dance with other women there. Kalipandi arrived at the temple under the influence of alcohol and created a ruckus with her. An upset Mariammal returned home with the children.Police said Mariammal allegedly locked the house from inside, poured kerosene on herself and the children, and set them on fire. Hearing their cries, neighbours rushed to the house, broke open a portion of the roof and extinguished the flames.Mariammal died at the spot, while her two sons, who sustained severe burns, were initially taken to Tenkasi Govt Hospital, and later shifted to Palayamkottai GH for advanced treatment. However, both children succumbed to their injuries one after another on Tuesday. Bodies were sent to the govt hospital for postmortem examination. articles.title: HC stays parking fee collection at Khammam Govt Hospital
articles.summary: Telangana High Court stays parking fee collection from patients and attendants at Khammam Govt District Hospital; counters sought, next hearing Nov 12.
articles.body: Hyderabad: Telangana high court on Thursday ordered an interim stay on collection of parking fee from patients and their attendants at Govt District Hospital, Khammam.Hearing a petition challenging parking fee collection at the health facility, Justice B Vijaysen Reddy ordered counters be filed by municipal administration and urban development department, director of medical education, Khammam collector and the hospital superintendent, while adjourning the case to Nov 12 for further hearing.The judge passed the directions while hearing a petition filed by Timmana Naveen Raju and Wazeed Mohmmad of Khammam town. Their counsel Ambedkar Dunna argued that authorities at the district hospital were collecting parking fee from patients and their attendants for vehicles parked on the hospital premises, terming the same as illegal, arbitrary and contrary to the rules.Ambedkar urged the court to initiate action against the respondent authorities for allegedly collecting parking fee exceeding municipality rules under the Telangana Apartments Act 1987 and Telangana Municipalities Act and also in violation of a GO governing parking fee collection issued by the MA&UD department in Feb 2018, and in further violation of the Right to Health guaranteed by the Constitution.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news.
